sources.entry: Deadbolt - Open-source file encryption tool. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/alichtman/deadbolt) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Deadbolt is an open-source desktop GUI and CLI tool for encrypting and decrypting files and folders with a password, built on Electron.
summary.what_it_does: Encrypts and decrypts files or folders using a password, through a desktop GUI or a command-line interface (installed via npm as deadbolt-cli). Encrypted files can be shared across macOS, Windows, and Linux. Encryption uses AES-256-GCM, with argon2id for password-based key derivation and the AES-GCM authentication tag for integrity checks. The file format has a version header: V002 (current) uses argon2id, while legacy V001 files (PBKDF2-SHA512) can still be decrypted. The CLI accepts a --password flag, or prompts for the password if none is given.
use_cases: Encrypting sensitive files before storing or sharing them
Password-protecting a folder on a laptop or desktop
Sharing encrypted files across macOS, Windows, and Linux
Decrypting .deadbolt files from the command line
Scripting file encryption with the CLI
how_to_run: Download AppImage, flatpak, .dmg, or .exe from the GitHub releases tab
npm install && npm run package:linux-flatpak (build flatpak from source)
notable: Cross-platform: encrypted files work across macOS, Windows, and Linux
Versioned file format (DEADBOLT_V002 header) with backward-compatible decryption of V001 files
Uses argon2id with RFC 9106 first-recommendation parameters (2 GiB memory, 1 iteration, 4 lanes)
Both a GUI app and a CLI (deadbolt-cli on npm)
caveats: CLI --password flag may leave the password in shell history
Auto-updates are not supported on Linux currently
Arch Linux AUR package (deadbolt-bin) is not maintained by the author
Version 2.0.0-beta shown in README build example; the argon2id change applies from v2.1.0-alpha onward
